headline: RBI mandates demat form and ₹1 crore minimum ticket size for securitisation notes
summary_points: RBI has issued Amendment Directions to the Commercial Banks - Securitisation Transactions Directions, 2025 under sections 21 and 35A of the BR Act, 1949.
Securitisation notes must be issued, held and transferred only in dematerialised form, with a minimum ticket size of ₹1 crore per investor.
Notes issued before April 1, 2027 will also have to comply with Paragraphs 27 and 28 for transactions after that date.

rows: Only dematerialised notes; minimum ₹1 crore at issuance and on every transfer
May be traded at amortised value even if ticket size falls below ₹1 crore
Size of investment by a single investor
Originator must ensure SPE agreement requires arrangements with registrar, depository, exchange etc.
Regulation 21 of SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations, 2008 to be complied with
Transactions in notes issued before April 1, 2027 must also follow Paragraphs 27 and 28

who_is_affected: Commercial banks acting as originators or investors in securitisation, SPEs, and investors dealing in securitisation notes.
action_required: Review SPE agreements and note structures, and put demat and ₹1 crore ticket-size arrangements in place before April 1, 2027, including for existing notes.

social.linkedin:
RBI has issued the Commercial Banks - Securitisation Transactions Amendment Directions, 2026 (RBI/2026-27/304, dated November 23, 2026), effective April 1, 2027.

Key changes to the 2025 Directions:

• Securitisation notes must be issued, held and transferred only in dematerialised form.
• Minimum ticket size is ₹1 crore at issuance and at every subsequent transfer, measured per single investor.
• Amortising notes may trade at amortised value even if the ticket falls below ₹1 crore.
• Originators must ensure SPE agreements provide for arrangements with registrars, depositories and exchanges to ensure compliance.
• Public offers must comply with Regulation 21 of the SEBI securitised debt instruments regulations.
• Transactions in notes issued before April 1, 2027 must also comply.

Banks, SPEs and investors should review existing structures and documentation well ahead of the effective date.

Please verify with the official RBI notification before acting.
